title: Atomic Structure and Radioactivity
seo_title: Year 9 Science: Atomic Structure and Radioactivity Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Explain how the model of the atom changed following the discovery of electrons, protons and neutrons and describe how natural radioactive decay results in stable atoms (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on atomic structure and radioactivity: models of the atom, protons, neutrons and electrons, atomic and mass numbers, isotopes, alpha, beta and gamma radiation and half-life. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons. Unstable nuclei decay to become stable.
body_html:
How to think about it

An atom has a tiny nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons around it.

  • The model changed with evidence: Dalton (solid atom) → Thomson (electrons) → Rutherford (nucleus) → Bohr (shells) → Chadwick (neutrons).
  • Atomic number = protons. Mass number = protons + neutrons. Isotopes have the same protons but different neutrons.
  • Unstable nuclei give off alpha, beta or gamma radiation. A half-life is the time for half the nuclei to decay.
Example

Sodium: atomic number 11, mass number 23. Neutrons?

23 − 11

Answer: 12

Example

800 atoms, 2 half-lives. Left?

800 → 400 → 200

Answer: 200

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the mass number is the number of neutrons.
  • Thinking isotopes are different elements.
  • Thinking all of a sample has decayed after two half-lives.

faq.q: Why did Rutherford's experiment change the model of the atom?
faq.a: Most alpha particles passed through gold foil but a few bounced back, so the atom must be mostly empty space with a tiny, dense, positive nucleus.

faq.q: What is the difference between alpha, beta and gamma radiation?
faq.a: Alpha particles are helium nuclei stopped by paper; beta particles are fast electrons stopped by thin aluminium; gamma rays are waves reduced by thick lead or concrete.

faq.q: How is radioactivity used in Australia?
faq.a: ANSTO at Lucas Heights makes radioisotopes for medical scans and cancer treatment, and radioactive dating helps scientists find the age of rocks and fossils.

items.q: A neon atom has the electron arrangement 2, 8. How many valence electrons does it have?
items.e: Valence electrons are in the outer shell.

items.q: What does 'random' mean for radioactive decay?
c: Every nucleus decays at the same time.
You cannot predict which nucleus will decay next or when.
It can be stopped by cooling.
items.e: Only the overall pattern is predictable.

items.q: What is activity?
c: the energy of an alpha particle
the rate at which a source of unstable nuclei decays, measured in becquerels (Bq)
items.e: 1 Bq = 1 decay per second.

items.q: What is the electron arrangement (shells) of a boron atom (5 electrons)?
items.e: Fill 2, then 8, then 8, then 2.

items.q: What does the mass number tell you?
c: the number of protons plus neutrons
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number.

items.q: Why did a few alpha particles bounce back from the gold foil?
c: They hit a tiny, dense, positive nucleus.
items.e: This led to the nuclear model of the atom.

items.q: What are valence electrons?
c: the electrons in the first shell
the electrons in the outermost shell
all the electrons in an atom
items.e: They decide how an atom reacts.

items.q: Why did the model of the atom change over time?
c: New experiments gave evidence that the old model could not explain.
Old scientists were wrong on purpose.
items.e: Science models improve with evidence.

items.q: In Rutherford's gold foil experiment, most alpha particles went straight through. What did this show?
c: Most of the atom is empty space.
items.e: A few bounced back, showing a small, dense nucleus.

items.q: Which particle has no charge?
items.e: Neutrons are neutral.

items.q: What is the radius of a nucleus compared with an atom?
c: about 1/10 000 of the radius of the atom
items.e: Mostly empty space.

items.q: What is radioactive decay?
c: an unstable nucleus giving out radiation to become more stable
an atom losing electrons in a reaction
items.e: Random process.

items.q: What does the atomic number tell you?
c: the number of protons in the nucleus
the mass of the atom in grams
the number of protons plus neutrons
items.e: It identifies the element.

items.q: What does the atomic number tell you?
items.e: It identifies the element.

items.q: Which particle has a positive charge?
items.e: Protons are +1.

items.q: Which type of radiation is stopped by a sheet of paper?
items.e: Alpha particles are large and heavily charged.

items.q: How many electron shells are occupied in a phosphorus atom?
items.e: 15 electrons: 2, 8, 5.

items.q: What is the mass number?
items.e: Particles in the nucleus.

items.q: How many electron shells are occupied in a beryllium atom?
items.e: 4 electrons: 2, 2.

items.q: ANSTO's reactor at Lucas Heights, Sydney, makes radioisotopes such as technetium-99m. What are they mainly used for?
items.e: Millions of patients use nuclear medicine.

items.q: How many more neutrons does <sup>134</sup>Cs have than <sup>133</sup>Cs?
A neutral atom of barium has a mass number of 140. How many electrons does it have?
items.e: In a neutral atom, electrons = protons = 56.

items.q: An atom has 5 neutrons and 3 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: Use the protons (3), not the neutrons.

items.q: An atom has 45 neutrons and 34 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: Use the protons (34), not the neutrons.

items.q: How many neutrons are in <sup>29</sup><sub>14</sub>Si?
An atom has 8 protons and 10 neutrons. What is its mass number?
An atom has 38 protons and 50 neutrons. What is its mass number?
What is a half-life?
c: half the time the atom exists
the time for all atoms to decay
the time for half of the radioactive atoms in a sample to decay
items.e: After each half-life, half of what is left decays.

items.q: How many protons are in an atom of magnesium-24?
items.e: The atomic number (12) is the number of protons.

items.q: Beryllium-9 and beryllium-10 are isotopes. What do they have the same number of?
items.e: Isotopes have the same protons but different neutrons.

items.q: An atom has 20 protons and 21 neutrons. What is its mass number?
A neutral atom of krypton has a mass number of 84. How many electrons does it have?
items.e: In a neutral atom, electrons = protons = 36.

items.q: A neutral atom of boron has a mass number of 12. How many electrons does it have?
items.e: In a neutral atom, electrons = protons = 5.

items.q: How many protons are in an atom of copper-65?
items.e: The atomic number (29) is the number of protons.

items.q: What are isotopes?
c: atoms with different numbers of protons
atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
items.e: Carbon-12 and carbon-14 are isotopes.

items.q: A neutral atom of sodium has a mass number of 25. How many electrons does it have?
items.e: In a neutral atom, electrons = protons = 11.

items.q: Sulfur-32 and sulfur-33 are isotopes. What do they have the same number of?
items.e: Isotopes have the same protons but different neutrons.

items.q: How many protons are in an atom of krypton-85?
items.e: The atomic number (36) is the number of protons.

items.q: Who discovered the neutron in 1932?
items.e: Neutrons explained the extra mass in the nucleus.

items.q: What is the electron arrangement (shells) of a silicon atom (14 electrons)?
items.e: Fill 2, then 8, then 8, then 2.

items.q: How many more neutrons does <sup>135</sup>Cs have than <sup>133</sup>Cs?
<sup>131</sup><sub>53</sub>I (iodine) undergoes beta decay. What nucleus forms?
items.e: Beta decay: mass number same, atomic number +1.

items.q: Which pair are isotopes of the same element?
items.e: Same atomic number, different mass numbers.

items.q: A nucleus has 70 protons and 64 neutrons. It undergoes beta decay. How many neutrons does the new nucleus have?
items.e: A neutron changes into a proton.

items.q: Which pair are isotopes of the same element?
items.e: Same atomic number, different mass numbers.

items.q: <sup>14</sup><sub>6</sub>C (carbon) undergoes beta decay. What nucleus forms?
items.e: Beta decay: mass number same, atomic number +1.

items.q: What stops alpha particles?
c: stopped by a few mm of aluminium
stopped by a sheet of paper or a few cm of air
reduced by thick lead or several metres of concrete
items.e: Alpha: most ionising, least penetrating. Gamma: least ionising, most penetrating.

items.q: A nucleus with mass number 241 and atomic number 95 emits an alpha particle. What are the mass number and atomic number of the new nucleus?
items.e: Alpha: mass −4, atomic −2. Beta: a neutron becomes a proton, so atomic +1 and mass unchanged.

items.q: <sup>40</sup><sub>19</sub>K (potassium) undergoes beta decay. What nucleus forms?
items.e: Beta decay: mass number same, atomic number +1.

items.q: A nucleus with mass number 118 undergoes alpha decay. What is the new mass number?
items.e: Alpha decay changes the mass number by -4.

items.q: <sup>90</sup><sub>38</sub>Sr (strontium) undergoes beta decay. What nucleus forms?
items.e: Beta decay: mass number same, atomic number +1.

items.q: <sup>60</sup><sub>27</sub>Co (cobalt) undergoes beta decay. What nucleus forms?
items.e: Beta decay: mass number same, atomic number +1.

items.q: How ionising are beta particles?
items.e: Alpha: most ionising, least penetrating. Gamma: least ionising, most penetrating.

items.q: What are beta particles?
items.e: Alpha: most ionising, least penetrating. Gamma: least ionising, most penetrating.

items.q: A nucleus with mass number 210 and atomic number 82 emits a beta particle. What are the mass number and atomic number of the new nucleus?
items.e: Alpha: mass −4, atomic −2. Beta: a neutron becomes a proton, so atomic +1 and mass unchanged.

items.q: What are gamma rays?
items.e: Alpha: most ionising, least penetrating. Gamma: least ionising, most penetrating.

items.q: What stops beta particles?
c: stopped by a sheet of paper or a few cm of air
reduced by thick lead or several metres of concrete
stopped by a few mm of aluminium
items.e: Alpha: most ionising, least penetrating. Gamma: least ionising, most penetrating.

items.q: A nucleus with mass number 234 and atomic number 92 emits an alpha particle. What are the mass number and atomic number of the new nucleus?
items.e: Alpha: mass −4, atomic −2. Beta: a neutron becomes a proton, so atomic +1 and mass unchanged.

items.q: What are alpha particles?
items.e: Alpha: most ionising, least penetrating. Gamma: least ionising, most penetrating.

items.q: A nucleus with mass number 230 and atomic number 90 emits an alpha particle. What are the mass number and atomic number of the new nucleus?
items.e: Alpha: mass −4, atomic −2. Beta: a neutron becomes a proton, so atomic +1 and mass unchanged.

items.q: How many half-lives pass when 96 g of strontium-90 decays to 12 g?
items.e: 96 g halves 3 times to reach 12 g.

items.q: What is alpha radiation made of?
items.e: Alpha: He nucleus; beta: electron; gamma: energy.

items.q: Which radiation is the most penetrating?
items.e: Needs lead or concrete.

items.q: In beta decay, what changes inside the nucleus?
c: A neutron changes into a proton and an electron is emitted.
items.e: Atomic number +1.

items.q: What fraction of a radioactive sample remains after 2 half-lives?
items.e: Halve 2 times.

items.q: What fraction of a radioactive sample remains after 4 half-lives?
items.e: Halve 4 times.

items.q: Noah has 480 g of caesium-137 (half-life 30 years). How much is left after 150 years?
items.e: 150 years = 5 half-lives: 480 → 15 g.

items.q: What is needed to stop gamma radiation?
c: a sheet of paper or skin
items.e: Alpha is least penetrating; gamma is most.

items.q: What is beta radiation made of?
items.e: Alpha: He nucleus; beta: electron; gamma: energy.

items.q: A sample has a count rate of 640 counts per minute. Its half-life is 8 minutes. What is the count rate after 16 minutes?
items.e: 16 minutes = 2 half-lives: halve 2 times.

items.q: A sample has a count rate of 1600 counts per minute. Its half-life is 12 hours. What is the count rate after 24 hours?
items.e: 24 hours = 2 half-lives: halve 2 times.

items.q: A sample has a count rate of 2400 counts per minute. Its half-life is 5 days. What is the count rate after 10 days?
items.e: 10 days = 2 half-lives: halve 2 times.

items.q: What is radioactive decay?
c: an unstable nucleus giving off particles or energy
items.e: Nucleus changes.

items.q: Ruby has 400 g of strontium-90 (half-life 29 years). How much is left after 87 years?
items.e: 87 years = 3 half-lives: 400 → 50 g.

items.q: Ruby has 160 g of iodine-131 (half-life 8 days). How much is left after 16 days?
items.e: 16 days = 2 half-lives: 160 → 40 g.

items.q: How ionising are gamma rays?
items.e: Alpha: most ionising, least penetrating. Gamma: least ionising, most penetrating.

items.q: What is the charge of gamma radiation?
items.e: Alpha +2, beta −1, gamma no charge.

items.q: What is the charge of alpha radiation?
items.e: Alpha +2, beta −1, gamma no charge.

items.q: A 480 g sample of caesium-137 (half-life 30 years) decays to 15 g. How much time has passed?
items.e: 5 half-lives × 30 years = 150 years.

items.q: What stops gamma rays?
c: stopped by a sheet of paper or a few cm of air
reduced by thick lead or several metres of concrete
stopped by a few mm of aluminium
items.e: Alpha: most ionising, least penetrating. Gamma: least ionising, most penetrating.

items.q: Chlorine's relative atomic mass is 35.45 u. Which isotope is more common?
items.e: The average is closer to 35.

items.q: A neutral atom of calcium has a mass number of 39. How many electrons does it have?
items.e: In a neutral atom, electrons = protons = 20.

items.q: Thomson discovered that atoms contain tiny negative particles. What were they?
items.e: Cathode ray experiments.

items.q: Kai tests 100 dice: each throw, dice showing 6 are 'decayed' and removed. What does this model?
items.e: Each atom has a fixed chance of decaying.

items.q: How many half-lives pass when 128 g of carbon-14 decays to 4 g?
items.e: 128 g halves 5 times to reach 4 g.

items.q: A smoke detector contains americium-241, an alpha emitter. Why is it safe in a room?
c: Alpha particles are stopped by air and the plastic case.
items.e: Low penetration.

items.q: Why do hospitals use technetium-99m (half-life 6 hours) for scans?
c: It gives off gamma rays and decays quickly, so little stays in the body.
items.e: Short half-life.

items.q: Ruby models an atom with a pea in the middle of a football field. What does the pea stand for?
c: the nucleus, which is tiny compared with the atom
items.e: The atom is mostly empty space.

items.q: How many protons are in an atom of neon-20?
items.e: The atomic number (10) is the number of protons.

items.q: Why is a radioisotope with a short half-life used for medical scans?
c: It decays quickly, so the patient is exposed for only a short time.
It lasts for years in the body.
items.e: Technetium-99m has a half-life of about 6 hours.

items.q: Kai has 64 g of caesium-137 (half-life 30 years). How much is left after 60 years?
items.e: 60 years = 2 half-lives: 64 → 16 g.

items.q: Why do elements in the same column have similar properties?
c: They have the same number of neutrons.
They have the same number of valence electrons.
items.e: Outer electrons decide reactions.

items.q: The count rate of a sample falls from 640 to 160 counts per minute. Its half-life is 8 days. How long did this take?
items.e: 2 half-lives.

items.q: Why do scientists measure the background radiation before an experiment?
c: to subtract it from the readings so only the source is measured
items.e: Background radiation comes from rocks, space and food.

items.q: Mia measures the count rate of a source: 400, 200, 100 counts per minute every 10 minutes. What is the half-life?
items.e: The count halves every 10 minutes.

items.q: What fraction of a radioactive sample remains after 3 half-lives?
items.e: Halve 3 times.

items.q: Why is carbon-14 used to date old wood but not dinosaur bones?
c: Its half-life (5730 years) is too short; almost none is left after millions of years.
items.e: Choose a fitting half-life.

items.q: Rutherford fired particles at gold foil. Most passed through, but a few bounced back. What did this show?
c: Atoms have a small, dense, positive nucleus and are mostly empty space.
items.e: The gold foil experiment.

items.q: How many neutrons are in <sup>107</sup><sub>47</sub>Ag?
Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5700 years. A bone has 1/4 of its original carbon-14. About how old is it?
items.e: 1/4 means two half-lives.
